# Results -- Study 252 (Search-Trends) on real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: each
month-end, standardise every stock's curated Google-Trends-style search interest
against its own trailing 6-month baseline (an attention z-score), LONG the
low-attention tercile, SHORT the high-attention tercile, hold 1 month and
rebalance. The reported spread is **low minus high** -- positive when the
Da-Engelberg-Gao (2011) attention->reversal ("fade the hype") effect pays.
Pinned against a random-portfolio control of the same tercile size.
**Proxy + survivorship-biased**: the attention series is a hand-curated proxy of
the public Google Trends shape, and the basket is 30 fixed mega-cap survivors --
all results are upper bounds.
As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (last row) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| yfinance monthly (adj close) | 2018-12-31 -> 2025-12-31 | 85 months x 29 tickers | `8c791a614b92` |
| Curated Trends-style attention | 2019-01-31 -> 2025-12-31 | 84 months x 30 tickers | hand-curated (deterministic) |

Basket: 29 tickers common to both tapes (SQ -> XYZ rename dropped). After the
6-month z-score burn-in and the min-stocks gate, **48 portfolio months**
(2019-11 -> 2025-11); ~10 names in each tercile, ~25 ranked per month.

## Primary specification (long low-attention / short high-attention, 1-month hold)

| Portfolio | Mean return | HAC *t* |
|-----------|------------|---------|
| Low-attention (long leg) | +1.9%/yr | +0.13 |
| High-attention (short leg) | **+79.1%/yr** | +1.31 |
| Equal-weight basket | +37.1%/yr | -- |
| **Spread (low - high)** | **-77.2%/yr = -642.9 bps/mo** | **-1.34** |

- The **spread is NEGATIVE** -- the *high*-attention (hyped) names *outperformed*
  the quiet ones, the **opposite** of the Da-Engelberg-Gao reversal hypothesis.
- The HAC **|t| = 1.34 < 2**: the effect is **not statistically significant** in
  either direction. The point estimate is dominated by the 2020-2021 meme/AI
  mania (GME, TSLA, NVDA, COIN) sitting in the high-attention tercile.
- The block-bootstrap 95% CI on the **spread Sharpe (ann): [-1.64, +0.02]**
  (97% of resamples negative) -- the reversal spread is, if anything, reliably
  *below* zero, confirming there is no fade-the-hype edge here.

## Sub-period analysis -- a sign-flip / sample-split artefact

| Period | Spread/yr | HAC *t* | n months |
|--------|-----------|---------|----------|
| 2019--2021 | -133.2%/yr | -1.04 | 21 |
| 2022--2025 |  -33.6%/yr | **-3.78** | 27 |

Both sub-periods are negative; the recent window even clears *t* = -2 (momentum,
not reversal). The headline reversal hypothesis is rejected across the sample.

## Tradability -- turnover, cost, and the short-leg borrow problem

| Cost assumption | Monthly drag | Net spread | Net *t* |
|-----------------|-------------|------------|---------|
| 15 bps one-way + 8 bps/mo borrow on the short | **35.7 bps/mo** | -81.4%/yr | -1.42 |

Costs are almost a footnote -- the *gross* spread is already the wrong sign. The
deeper problem: the SHORT leg is the meme tercile (GME, AMC, COIN, RIVN, LCID),
i.e. exactly the hard-to-borrow, squeeze-prone names where 8 bps/mo borrow is
wildly optimistic and a single squeeze can wipe the book.

## Random-portfolio null

A random tercile-sized group earns ~ -20 bps/mo mean excess (within sampling
noise of zero given a ~1500 bps/draw std driven by fat meme-stock tails). The
attention sort extracts no reliable cross-sectional information on this panel.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds the effect when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) the engine recovers
the planted attention->reversal premium monotonically:

| Planted premium | Spread mean/yr | Spread HAC *t* |
|----------------|---------------|----------------|
| 0.00 (null)    | (sampling noise) | -2.32 (one null draw; |t|<4 expected) |
| +0.03          | +59.3%/yr      | **+12.61**     |
| +0.05          | +106.1%/yr     | **+21.90**     |

The engine is truthful: a planted fade-the-hype premium yields a strongly
positive, significant spread. The real tape simply carries no such signal.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The literature (Da-Engelberg-Gao 2011) documents a genuine
  attention->reversal effect at weekly horizon on a broad retail-held universe.
  But on this monthly, mega-cap, proxy-Trends tape the (low-high) spread is
  -77%/yr at HAC *t* = -1.34 -- the **wrong sign and not significant**. Per the
  desk rubric, literature support *without* a robust HAC *t* >= 2 on the real
  tape is **WEAK**, not REAL.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The gross spread is already wrong-signed; the short
  leg is un-shortable meme names with punitive borrow and squeeze risk; the
  attention series is a hand-curated proxy; the sample is 30 survivor mega-caps
  over just 48 portfolio months. Nothing here is implementable. **MIRAGE**.
- **Survivorship + proxy -- named.** The basket is fixed survivors and the
  attention table is a stylised hand-curated approximation of Google Trends; all
  results are upper bounds on a real, broad-universe, true-SVI implementation.
